name: Duane Retraction Syndrome with Congenital Deafness
aliases: Duane Syndrome with Congenital Hearing Loss
Duane Retraction Syndrome Type with Sensorineural Deafness

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Duane Retraction Syndrome with Congenital Deafness

criteria.description: Congenital limitation of horizontal eye movement, especially abduction
Globe retraction and narrowing of palpebral fissure on attempted adduction
Bilateral or unilateral congenital sensorineural hearing loss
No evidence of other cranial nerve palsies or systemic neurological deficits
MRI demonstrating absence or hypoplasia of the abducens nerve

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital limitation of horizontal eye movement with globe retraction plus congenital sensorineural deafness, supported by imaging findings if available.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging and audiological testing support confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital limitation of horizontal eye abduction
Globe retraction with palpebral fissure narrowing on adduction
searchTerms: eye pulls back with eyelid narrowing
eyelid slit narrows when eye moves
hearing loss from birth due to nerve damage
born with inner ear hearing impairment
strabismus with inward or outward turning

common.symptomName: Head turn or face turn to compensate for limited eye movement
searchTerms: head tilt to adjust for eye movement

common.symptomName: Mild to moderate speech delay due to hearing impairment
searchTerms: speech delay due to hearing loss
hearing asymmetry one or both sides
one side of face slightly different

occasional.symptomName: Mild developmental delay unrelated to hearing loss
searchTerms: mild developmental delay not from hearing

rare.symptomName: Other cranial nerve palsies (e.g., facial nerve involvement)

imaging: MRI showing absence or hypoplasia of the abducens nerve
Orbital imaging demonstrating globe retraction on adduction
other: Clinical observation of abnormal eye movements and hearing assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Bilateral facial and abducens nerve palsy
Isolated sixth nerve palsy without globe retraction
Facial asymmetry with ear and vertebral anomalies

redFlags: Sudden onset of diplopia or eye movement limitation
Presence of additional cranial nerve deficits or systemic neurological signs
